title: Terminal-site evaluation identifies ordinary modules and derived scalar extension
statement: Let $\mathcal T$ be the category with one object $*$ and only its identity arrow, equipped with the topology whose sole covering sieve is the maximal sieve. For a commutative ring $A$, let $\underline A$ be the ring sheaf on $\mathcal T$ with value $A$. Evaluation $E_A:\operatorname{Mod}(\underline A)\to A\text{-}\operatorname{Mod}$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] is an exact equivalence, with inverse assigning a module its one-object sheaf. It identifies sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] with ordinary module tensor [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], including its action on morphisms, and identifies direct-sum total tensors, cohomology, quasi-isomorphisms and K-flat complexes [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-module-kflat-complex]. Termwise evaluation therefore induces equivalences $K(\underline A)\simeq K(A)$ and $D(\underline A)\simeq D(A)$, compatible with the localization functors [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For any homomorphism $f:A\to A'$, these equivalences identify termwise sheaf change of rings along $\underline f$ with ordinary extension of scalars $-\otimes_A A'$ [def-weil-module-base-change]. They transport the universal total left derived pair (functor and its natural counit) [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class] of the former to a universal total left derived pair of the latter. In particular the derived change of rings of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] becomes ordinary derived scalar extension, with the same resolution computation isomorphisms and derived-to-ordinary counit. No flatness of $f$ or boundedness of complexes is assumed.

source.place: Tag 03CW (definition-sheaf-modules), specialized to the category with one object, one arrow, and only the maximal covering sieve; the exact tensor equivalence and the transport of localization and universal derived pairs are the explicit terminal-site specialization of these definitions.

proof.text: On $\mathcal T$, a presheaf is determined by its value at $*$: its only restriction is the identity. A matching family on the maximal sieve consists of one element $x$ at the identity arrow, and its unique amalgamation is $x$. Thus every presheaf is a sheaf. By [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], a $\underline A$-module sheaf is precisely an $A$-module at $*$, and a sheaf morphism is precisely an $A$-linear map there. Define $I_A(M)(*)=M$, with identity restriction, and define $I_A(u)$ by its sole component $u$. Then $E_AI_A=1$ and the map $I_AE_A\mathcal F\to\mathcal F$ whose component is the identity is a natural isomorphism. Both inverse identities are identities at the only object. This constructs the asserted equivalence.

source.place: Tag 03CW (definition-sheaf-modules), explicit matching-family computation for the maximal sieve on the singleton identity category

proof.text: Kernels in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] are sectionwise, and cokernels are sheafified sectionwise cokernels. Step 1 makes that sheafification the identity up to its canonical isomorphism. Thus $E_A$ and $I_A$ preserve kernels, cokernels and hence images and exact sequences: exactness here is exactly ordinary module exactness. For any family $(M_i)$, the one-object sheaf with value $\bigoplus_iM_i$, with the usual inclusions, is a coproduct: a sheaf map out of it is exactly a linear map from that direct sum, hence exactly a family of linear maps from the $M_i$. Evaluation therefore also identifies arbitrary direct sums, including the empty direct sum.

source.place: Tags 03CW and 03DA (lemma-abelian), with sectionwise kernels/cokernels and the direct-sum universal property on this site

proof.text: By [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], $\mathcal F\otimes_{\underline A}\mathcal G$ is the sheafification of the presheaf with sole value $\mathcal F(*)\otimes_A\mathcal G(*)$. It is already a sheaf by step 1. The comparison with ordinary tensor sends the section represented by $x\otimes y$ to $x\otimes y$. For maps $u,v$, both tensor maps send this generator to $u(x)\otimes v(y)$; generation and uniqueness in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] make the square commute. The inverse comparison has the same formula. These formulas also identify the unit $\underline A$ with $A$ and all iterated tensor comparisons: the two possible composites act identically on pure tensors.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), the two displayed tensor definitions, evaluated at the unique object

proof.text: The equivalence in step 1 preserves zero maps, since its action on morphisms is evaluation. Apply [lem-weil-equivalence-map-homological-complex] to obtain inverse termwise equivalences on integer-indexed cochain complexes. Their differentials are exactly $E_A(d^n)$ and $I_A(d^n)$. By [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], a total tensor has degree $n$ equal to $\bigoplus_{p+q=n}\mathcal F^p\otimes\mathcal G^q$ and differential $d_{\mathcal F}\otimes1+(-1)^p1\otimes d_{\mathcal G}$. Steps 2 and 3 identify each summand and both differential terms with the corresponding module maps. Consequently the degreewise tensor comparison is a natural chain isomorphism of the direct-sum total tensors, even for unbounded complexes.

source.place: Section 06YL (section-flat), direct-sum tensor complex; termwise equivalence: Mathlib Algebra/Homology/Additive.lean:224-232

proof.text: By the formula $H^n(K)=\ker(d^n)/\operatorname{im}(d^{n-1})$ in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], step 2 gives $E_AH^n(K)\cong H^n(E_AK)$, naturally in chain maps, and the inverse functor gives the reverse identification. Thus acyclicity and quasi-isomorphisms correspond in both directions. Every acyclic module complex is $E_AI_AF$ for an acyclic sheaf complex $I_AF$. Using the total tensor comparison of step 4, the assertion that $\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes K)$ is acyclic for every acyclic $F$ is consequently identical on the two sides. This is exactly K-flatness in [def-pc-kflat-complex] and [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]; the same observation identifies K-flat resolutions.

source.place: Definition 06YN (definition-K-flat), compared directly with more-algebra.tex Definition 06XZ

proof.text: In the homotopy category, cochain maps $u,v:K\to L$ are identified when there are maps $h^n:K^n\to L^{n-1}$ satisfying $u^n-v^n=d_L^{n-1}h^n+h^{n+1}d_K^n$. Evaluation and its inverse preserve this equality termwise, including its sums and compositions. They therefore give inverse functors $e_A:K(\underline A)\rightleftarrows K(A):i_A$ with the same termwise unit and counit. This proves the homotopy-category equivalence. The shift and the cone matrices in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] are also preserved termwise, because both functors preserve sums, negatives and the differentials.

source.place: Section 05RN (section-homotopy), explicit degree-minus-one homotopy equation; shift and cone formulas of the homotopy category

proof.text: Write $Q_s:K(\underline A)\to D(\underline A)$ and $Q_m:K(A)\to D(A)$ for localization. By step 5, $Q_me_A$ and $Q_si_A$ invert quasi-isomorphisms. Parts (1) and (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] give $d_A:D(\underline A)\to D(A)$ and $j_A:D(A)\to D(\underline A)$ with $d_AQ_s\cong Q_me_A$ and $j_AQ_m\cong Q_si_A$. They also lift the unit and counit of $e_A\dashv i_A$ to $1\cong j_Ad_A$ and $d_Aj_A\cong1$. Their inverse and triangle equations hold after precomposition with $Q_s$ or $Q_m$, since there they are the equations in step 6; part (3) makes them hold on the derived categories. Hence $d_A,j_A$ are the desired inverse derived equivalences, with the stated localization comparisons.

source.place: Definition 05RU (definition-unbounded-derived-category); categories.tex Tags 04VG/04VK, with the natural-transformation localization property stated in the cited node

proof.text: Fix $f:A\to A\prime$. Denote termwise sheaf change of rings by $T_s$ and module extension of scalars by $T_m$. Steps 1 and 3 identify the value of $T_s\mathcal F$ with $\mathcal F(*)\otimes_A A\prime$. The $A\prime$-action sends $x\otimes b$ to $x\otimes ab$, and the map induced by $u$ sends $x\otimes b$ to $u(x)\otimes b$. These are precisely the object, scalar-action and morphism formulas of [def-weil-module-base-change]. Thus the identity on these tensors gives $e_{A\prime}T_s\cong T_me_A$ on homotopy categories; differential compatibility is the same termwise formula. Here $T_s$ is the sheaf change of rings of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].

source.place: Tag 03EK, change of rings; algebra.tex Tag 05G3 (section-base-change), including the tensor formula on morphisms

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class] on $\mathcal T$ with $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(\underline A)$, the functor $F_s=Q_s'T_s:K(\underline A)\to D(\underline{A'})$ and the class $\mathcal P$ of K-flat sheaf complexes [def-pc-kflat-complex]; primes denote the target ring, and likewise $F_m=Q_m'T_m$. Exactness of $F_s$: $T_s$ is additive termwise (step 8), so it commutes with the shift and carries the cone matrices of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] to those of $T_sf$; $Q_s'$ commutes with shifts and sends cone triangles to distinguished triangles by that definition. Hypothesis (1): [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] gives every sheaf complex a K-flat resolution. Hypothesis (2): a quasi-isomorphism of $K(\underline A)$ between K-flat complexes is represented by a chain quasi-isomorphism; clause (1) of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], applied to $\underline f:\underline A\to\underline{A'}$ (sheaves of commutative rings on the site $\mathcal T$, step 1), makes its $T_s$ image a quasi-isomorphism, so its $F_s$ image is invertible. The lemma gives a universal pair $(L_s,\varepsilon_s:L_sQ_s\to F_s)$ with $\varepsilon_{s,P}$ invertible for every K-flat $P$. Clause (2) of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] is the left derived functor of the same $F_s$; a universal pair is unique up to the unique isomorphism compatible with the counits, so $L_s$ is that derived change of rings, and its resolution isomorphism for a K-flat resolution $q$ is $\varepsilon_{s,P}\circ L_s(Q_sq)^{-1}$. No flatness of $f$ or boundedness of complexes is assumed.

source.place: Tag 06XN (lemma-find-existence-computes), dual part, applied as in sites-cohomology.tex Tag 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change) proof; K-flat resolutions as in lem-pc-kflat-resolution

proof.text: Define $L_m=d_{A\prime}L_sj_A$. For a module complex $M$, define $\gamma_M:L_mQ_mM\to F_mM$ by the composite $d_{A\prime}L_sj_AQ_mM\cong d_{A\prime}L_sQ_si_AM\xrightarrow{d_{A\prime}(\varepsilon_{s,i_AM})}d_{A\prime}F_si_AM\cong F_mM$. The first comparison is step 7; the last uses steps 7 and 8 and $e_Ai_A\cong1$. Each comparison and $\varepsilon_s$ is natural, so these arrows form a natural transformation $\gamma:L_mQ_m\to F_m$. This specifies the transported counit, rather than merely an isomorphism between the values of two functors.

source.place: Tag 05S9 and equation-everywhere: direct conjugation of the universal pair, using the explicit localization comparisons

proof.text: To check universality, let $H:D(A)\to D(A\prime)$ be any functor. The inverse equivalences in step 7 and their units/counits give bijections $\operatorname{Nat}(H,L_m)\cong\operatorname{Nat}(j_{A\prime}Hd_A,L_s)$ and $\operatorname{Nat}(j_{A\prime}Hd_AQ_s,F_s)\cong\operatorname{Nat}(HQ_m,F_m)$: apply the inverse functors to components and insert the unit/counit isomorphisms, reversing with the forward functors. These operations are inverse by the two triangle identities; for the second bijection also substitute $d_AQ_s\cong Q_me_A$ and $d_{A\prime}F_s\cong F_me_A$, then precompose with $i_A$. Between these bijections, the universal property in [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class] sends $\beta:j_{A\prime}Hd_A\to L_s$ to $\varepsilon_s\circ(\beta Q_s)$. By the formula of step 10, the resulting composite sends $\alpha:H\to L_m$ precisely to $\gamma\circ(\alpha Q_m)$. This proves the required bijection for every $H$, hence $(L_m,\gamma)$ is a universal total left derived pair for ordinary scalar extension.

source.place: Universal-pair convention of Tag 05S9 and equation-everywhere; explicit natural-transformation bijection using the already constructed inverse equivalences

proof.text: Let $q:P\to M$ be any ordinary K-flat resolution. Step 5 makes $i_Aq$ a K-flat sheaf resolution. By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] and the K-flat counit clause of [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class], $\gamma_P$ is invertible, and so is $L_m(Q_mq)$. The resolution computation is therefore $L_m(Q_mM)\xrightarrow{L_m(Q_mq)^{-1}}L_m(Q_mP)\xrightarrow{\gamma_P}Q_m\prime(T_mP)$. This is exactly evaluation of the sheaf resolution computation. Naturality gives $\gamma_M=F_m(q)\circ\gamma_P\circ L_m(Q_mq)^{-1}$, so its derived-to-ordinary comparison is the same localized tensor-augmentation map. Comparisons between two resolutions are the composites of these isomorphisms, hence their cocycle identities are preserved too. For an object placed in degree zero this identifies $M\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A\prime\to(M\otimes_AA\prime)[0]$ with the sheaf counit. All constructions above use the full unbounded categories and make no flatness assumption.
